title: Private node autorepair orchestration & health-signal routing playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Runbook + automation spec for automated remediation of common Private (VPC) node health failures. Focuses on signal routing, safe Terraform reconciliation, node replacement orchestration, and observable safeguards to avoid cascading repairs in multi-tenant private deployments. This playbook is intended for SRE/infra on-call engineers and the automation pipeline (CI/CD) that executes ephemeral repairs or escalates to human intervention.
steps: 1) Triage: Identify primary failing signal (healthprobe down, SSM unreachable, ENI detach, route/peer flaps, kubelet crashloop). Use telemetry queries to classify impact and scope (single node / subnet / AZ / all nodes in private cluster).

2) Signal routing: Map symptom -> remediation track. Examples: kubelet crashloop -> graceful pod evacuation + node replace; ENI detach -> attempt ENI reattach flow; SSM unreachable + control plane unreachable -> escalate to human.

3) Observe precondition: Check terraform remote state workspace lock, last apply timestamp, and drift score (calculated by drift detector lambda). Refuse automated apply if a lock or active manual change detected.

4) Safe plan: Run terraform plan in a read-only environment (CI job) with -target limited to affected module(s). Emit plan diff to the alert thread and to Ops dashboard. If plan is empty, prefer node-level fixes; if plan proposes deletions, require manual approval.

5) Evacuate workload: If affecting serving nodes, reroute traffic (circuit-breaker) by adding node to 'drain' group via console API and/or set service-level fallback to Hosted or Dedicated as configured.

6) Node repair paths (ordered): a) soft restart of kubelet/agent via SSM cloud-init command; b) reattach ENI and re-run dhclient/network restart; c) taint node and spawn replacement via ASG/instance-pool lifecycle hook; d) recreate node via terraform apply on node module if instance metadata corrupted.
7) Apply remediation in CI with canary: pick one node in the same AZ, run automated repair, watch for regressions for 10 minutes, then sweep remainder if canary successful.

8) Post-repair verification: Run end-to-end health checks (prefix KV cache tests, tokenized inference baseline, API latency spike test). Verify metrics back to normal for at least 5m before marking incident resolved.

9) Audit & state: Commit remediation run output (terraform plan/apply logs, SSM command output, node lifecycle events) to secured incident log (S3) and append to incident ticket. Ensure remote state version increment is recorded.

10) Escalate: If automated attempts fail after two retries or if remediation changes > threshold (deletions or >3 nodes in AZ), set status to "Human Required" and page on-call infra with runbook digest.

automation_playbook: Detection: Alert rule triggered in CloudWatch/Prometheus -> webhook to Incident Orchestrator (Lambda) -> enrich with last-successful-apply and drift-score.
Decision: Orchestrator decides track = {node_repair, network_fix, escalate} based on symptom tags and drift-score. If drift-score > 0.5 or workspace locked -> escalate to human.

Canary: If track=node_repair, Orchestrator selects single canary node (prefer older AMI, same AZ) and forks a CI job to run the targeted terraform plan -> optional taint -> instance replacement. CI job runs under limited runtime role and publishes logs to S3 with KMS encryption.
Guardrails: Every automated apply must satisfy: plan_size <= 3 resources changed, no resource deletions > 0, required_tags intact. If guardrail fails, abort and page.
Rollback: For any automated change, capture snapshots (AMIs, EBS snapshots) before apply. If post-check fails, run the reverse sequence (recreate old instance from AMI and reattach).
Escalation: If canary fails twice or more than 2 nodes need repair in same AZ, set cluster to degraded mode and trigger on-call paging with runbook summary.
Audit: All automation decisions and artifacts are pushed to the incident ticket and to the compliance S3 bucket with Customer-ID tagging for private deployments.
Rate-limiting: Limit automated repairs to 1 node per AZ per 10 minutes to avoid cascading replacements during large network events.
telemetry_queries: CloudWatch alarm: Sum(ENI.Detach) > 0 in 1m for subnet-id
CloudWatch: metric 'SSM/Agent/Heartbeats' sparse window: count(Heartbeat) by instance < 1 over 5m
Drift lambda: SELECT resource, diff_score FROM drift_report WHERE env='private' AND diff_score>0.2
notes: Key difference from prior runbooks: this playbook prioritizes signal classification + terraform-safe reconciliation guards before any destructive changes.
We use a canary-first approach to reduce blast radius for Private customers where network policies and customer-managed routing can create asymmetric failures.
Ensure provider versions are pinned in module root to avoid unexpected provider behavior during automated apply (example: aws ~> 4.40).
